gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.

gaps.sentence: We had a ___ of fun at the fair.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of fun' is the fixed phrase; 'fun' is uncountable and the article 'a' forces 'lot'.
'Several charges' means more than two; the other options are used only with uncountable nouns.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ money, so he couldn't even buy a bus ticket.
gaps.explanation: 'Had no money' states zero and explains the result; 'none' cannot stand directly before a noun.

gaps.sentence: The ___ of teenagers own a smartphone these days.
gaps.explanation: 'The majority of + plural noun' means most of them; 'the number of teenagers own' would be ungrammatical.

gaps.sentence: She's very fussy — she refuses to eat ___ green.
gaps.hint: after 'refuse' the clause is negative in meaning
gaps.explanation: Verbs like refuse, deny and avoid create a negative context, so 'anything' is used.

gaps.sentence: She has two children. One lives in Leeds, and ___ lives in York.
gaps.hint: one of a pair of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... the other ...' is the pattern for exactly two; 'another' would imply more than two.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the equipment has been serviced this year, so breakdowns are rare.
gaps.explanation: 'Most of + noun' = the majority of it; 'the most' is a superlative.
